svg.title: Figure 3. Load sharing with a fit-up gap (illustrative)
svg.desc: Two plots for an illustrative brass rod in a steel tube with a 0.12 millimeter gap, press load 0 to 60 kN. Left: member 2's force stays at zero in a shaded region up to the load k1 times g, about 12 kN, then becomes increasingly compressive along a straight line; a dashed line through the origin shows the no-gap prediction with a constant share; member 1's force is the dash-dot line and carries all the load until the gap closes. The shaded region is labeled superposition fails in the shaded range. Right: the caps' approach rises steeply with slope 1 over k1 plus C until the gap closes, then more gently with slope 1 over k1 plus k2, plus C, where C is the compliance of the caps and fixtures.
